line: Make ’em crack, no arm and hammer, it’s sorta like armageddon
vault_lines: Make 'em crack, no arm and hammer, it's sorta like armageddon
meaning:
Arm & Hammer is a brand of baking-soda-based consumer products. Therefore, “make ‘em crack” has two meanings:


Doja is saying that she is greatly harming her critics thus making them “crack” as in break. A literal arm and a hammer would be able to crack an object and Doja’s lack of them symbolizes how she can hurt them effortlessly.
“Make ‘em crack” could also mean “convert them into crack”. As seen in the picture displayed in this CBC article, Arm & Hammer products can be used to convert cocaine into crack. Doja could also be using “make ‘em crack” to mean “make crack for them” to imply they’re so hurt they need crack to cope.



https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/crack-cocaine-9-things-to-know-1.2415886

That being said, she’s comparing how she makes her critics crack without the need of an arm and hammer to making crack with Arm & Hammer products.

Doja then proceeds to play on the word “arm” in “Armageddon”. Armageddon is the mythological ultimate war between the forces of good and the forces of evil and is associated with chaos and intense war. Doja uses this to represent and mock the overreaction of her critics.

Overall, Doja masterfully uses a double entendre, wordplay and a simile in one line to describe how she can anger her critics with ease.
